1. [EPA-HQ-OPP-2026-4192; FRL-13655-01-OCSPP]

# AGENCY:

Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

# ACTION:

Notice.

# SUMMARY:

Pursuant to the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is hereby issuing an order for the cancellations of the pesticide product registrations identified in this document. EPA previously announced its receipt of and requested comments on requests to voluntarily cancel the product registrations listed in Table 1 of Unit II. and announced its intent to cancel the product registrations listed in Table 3 of Unit III. With the issuance of this cancellation order, any sale, distribution, or use of products listed in this notice will be permitted after the registrations have been cancelled only if such sale, distribution, or use is consistent with the terms as described in the final order.

# DATES:

These cancellations are effective November 13, 2026.

# ADDRESSES:

 The docket for this action, identified by docket identification (ID) number EPA-HQ-OPP-2026-4192, is available through https://www.regulations.gov. Additional information about dockets generally, along with instructions for visiting the docket in person, is available at https://www.epa.gov/​dockets.

# FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:

 Jennifer Drobish, Regulatory & Information Services Division (7505M), Office of Mission Critical Operations, Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20460-0001; telephone number: (202) 202-2642; email address: drobish.jennifer@epa.gov.

# SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

## I. Executive Summary

### A. Does this action apply to me?

This action is directed to the public in general and may be of interest to a wide range of stakeholders including environmental, human health, and agricultural advocates; the chemical industry; pesticide users; and members of the public interested in the sale, distribution, or use of pesticides. Since others also may be interested, the Agency has not attempted to describe all the specific entities that may be affected by this action.

### B. What is EPA's authority for taking this action?

 FIFRA section 6(f)(1) (7 U.S.C. 136d(f)(1)) provides that a registrant of a pesticide product may at any time request that any of its pesticide registrations be cancelled or amended to terminate one or more uses. FIFRA further provides that, before acting on the request, EPA must publish a notice of receipt of any such request in the Federal Register . Thereafter, following the public comment period, the EPA Administrator may approve such a request. 

FIFRA section 4(i)(5) (7 U.S.C. 136a-1(i)(5)) requires that all pesticide registrants pay an annual registration maintenance fee, due by January 15 of each year, to keep their registrations in effect. This requirement applies to all registrations granted under FIFRA section 3 (7 U.S.C. 136a) as well as those granted under FIFRA section 24(c) (7 U.S.C. 136v(c)) to meet special local needs. Registrations for which the fee is not paid are subject to cancellation by order and without hearing. Under FIFRA, the EPA Administrator may reduce or waive maintenance fees for minor agricultural use pesticides when it is determined that the fee would be likely to have significant impact on the availability of pesticides for the use.

### C. What action is the Agency taking?

This cancellation order follows a notice of receipt and opportunity for public comments on the requests from the registrants listed to voluntarily cancel their product registrations. See 91 FR 38423, June 25, 2026 (FRL-13402-01-OCSPP). In that document, EPA also provided a notice of intent to cancel certain other product registrations for non-payment of the 2026 pesticide registration maintenance fees. Since registrations for which the fee is not paid are subject to cancellation by order and without hearing, EPA did not seek public comment for the cancellation of the products listed.

In that document, EPA indicated that it would issue an order implementing the cancellations, unless the Agency received substantive comments within the 30-day comment period that would merit its further review of the requests, or unless the registrants withdrew their requests. The Agency received three comments, two of which were requests from companies listed in Table 3 to move to Table 1. The Agency agrees and has granted those requests. Accordingly, EPA hereby issues this cancellation order granting the requested cancellations. Any distribution, sale, or use of the products subject to this cancellation order is permitted only in accordance with the terms of this order, including any existing stocks provisions.

## II. Cancellation Order

 Pursuant to FIFRA section 6(f) (7 U.S.C. 136d(f)), EPA hereby approves the requested cancellations and orders that the product registrations identified in Table 1 of this unit are cancelled. The effective date of the cancellations that are the subject of this order is November 13, 2026. Any distribution, sale, or use of existing stocks of the products ( printed page 73230) identified in Table 1 of this unit in a manner inconsistent with any of the provisions for disposition of existing stocks set forth in Unit VII. will be a violation of FIFRA. 

Table 1 of this unit lists the product cancellations, as requested by registrants, in sequence by registration number (or company number and FIFRA section 24(c) number).

# SUMMARY:

Pursuant to the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is hereby issuing an order for the cancellations of the pesticide product registrations identified in this document. EPA previously announced its receipt of and requested comments on requests to voluntarily cancel the product registrations listed in Table 1 of Unit II. and announced its intent to cancel the product registrations listed in Table 3 of Unit III. With the issuance of this cancellation order, any sale, distribution, or use of products listed in this notice will be permitted after the registrations have been cancelled only if such sale, distribution, or use is consistent with the terms as described in the final order.

# DATES:

These cancellations are effective November 13, 2026.

...

FIFRA section 4(i)(5) (7 U.S.C. 136a-1(i)(5)) requires that all pesticide registrants pay an annual registration maintenance fee, due by January 15 of each year, to keep their registrations in effect. This requirement applies to all registrations granted under FIFRA section 3 (7 U.S.C. 136a) as well as those granted under FIFRA section 24(c) (7 U.S.C. 136v(c)) to meet special local needs. Registrations for which the fee is not paid are subject to cancellation by order and without hearing. Under FIFRA, the EPA Administrator may reduce or waive maintenance fees for minor agricultural use pesticides when it is determined that the fee would be likely to have significant impact on the availability of pesticides for the use.

...

Any distribution, sale, or use of the products subject to this cancellation order is permitted

...

Pursuant to FIFRA section 6(f) (7 U.S.C. 136d(f)), EPA hereby approves the requested cancellations and orders that the product registrations identified in Table 1 of this unit are cancelled. The effective date of the cancellations that are the subject of this order is November 13, 2026. Any distribution, sale, or use of existing stocks of the products ( printed page 73230) identified in Table 1 of this unit in a manner inconsistent with any of the provisions for disposition of existing stocks set forth in Unit VII. will be a violation of FIFRA. 

Table 1 of this unit lists the product cancellations, as requested by registrants, in sequence by registration number (or company number and FIFRA section 24(c) number).

...

Table 3 of this unit lists all the FIFRA sections 3 and 24(c) registrations that are canceled for non-payment of the 2026 maintenance fee. These registrations are canceled by this order effective November 13, 2026 and without hearing.

Table 3—Registrations Cancelled for Non-Payment of 2026 Maintenance Fee

| Registration No. | Company No. | Product name | Active ingredient |

...

Existing stocks are those stocks of registered pesticide products which are currently in the United States, and which were packaged, labeled, and released for shipment prior to the effective date of the cancellation action. The existing stocks provisions for the products subject to this order are as follows.

The registrants may continue to sell and distribute existing stocks of products listed in Table 1 of Unit II. until January 15, 2027. Thereafter, the registrants are prohibited from selling or distributing products listed in Table 1 of Unit II., except for export in accordance with FIFRA section 17 (7 U.S.C. 136o), or proper disposal. People other than the registrants may sell, distribute, or use existing stocks of products listed in Table 1 of Unit II. until existing stocks are exhausted, provided that such sale, distribution, or use is consistent with the terms of the previously approved labeling on, or that accompanied, the canceled products.

calls.prompt:
Convert your research below into the required list. Keep exactly the items and facts you found; do not add new ones.

Task was:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if a deadline is < 90 days from 2026-11-13, otherwise High/Medium/Low by importance), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

Your research:
Found **9 company-relevant documents**. Dates below are assessed from **2026-11-13**; “Critical—immediate” denotes an obligation already in effect.

1. **FR Doc. 2026-23112 — [Revocation of the Color Additive Listing for Use of Orange B on Casings or Surfaces of Frankfurters and Sausages; Confirmation of Effective Date](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23112/revocation-of-the-color-additive-listing-for-use-of-orange-b-on-casings-or-surfaces-of-frankfurters)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-13 | **Key deadline:** Effective **2026-09-08**, now confirmed | **Tier:** **Critical—immediate**  
   **Owner:** food-safety — Maria Chen  
   **Reason:** FDA confirmed that Orange B is no longer authorized on frankfurter or sausage casings/surfaces, directly affecting Brightside’s meat products.  
   **Action:** Immediately verify formulas, casing specifications, supplier declarations and inventory; remove and document disposition of any Orange B-containing materials.

2. **FR Doc. 2026-22866 — [Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22866/color-additive-petition-from-the-international-association-of-color-manufacturers-request-to-amend)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-10 | **Key deadline:** Objections/hearing requests due **2026-12-10**; order scheduled effective **2027-01-11** | **Tier:** **Critical**  
   **Owner:** food-safety — Maria Chen  
   **Reason:** The order removes authorization for these solvents in manufacturing annatto extract, paprika oleoresin and turmeric oleoresin used as food colors.  
   **Action:** Obtain supplier manufacturing declarations, revise color specifications and qualify compliant replacements before the effective date; file any justified objection by December 10.

3. **FR Doc. 2026-22865 — [Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22865/color-additive-petition-from-environmental-defense-fund-et-al-request-to-amend-the-color-additive)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-10 | **Key deadline:** Objections/hearing requests due **2026-12-10**; order scheduled effective **2027-01-11** | **Tier:** **Critical**  
   **Owner:** food-safety — Maria Chen  
   **Reason:** This companion order separately removes methylene chloride as a diluent in color-additive mixtures used in fruit-and-vegetable marking inks.  
   **Action:** Check produce and color-ink suppliers for the affected use and incorporate its removal into the FR Doc. 2026-22866 compliance review.

4. **FR Doc. 2026-22944 — [Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22944/modification-to-work-requirements-for-able-bodied-adults)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-10 | **Key deadline:** Comments due **2026-12-10** | **Tier:** **Critical**  
   **Owner:** sales — Aisha Grant  
   **Reason:** Proposed SNAP time-limit exceptions, age coverage and geographic-waiver changes could alter customer eligibility and SNAP-supported demand.  
   **Action:** Model Ohio/Georgia sales exposure under the proposed eligibility scenarios and submit demand-impact comments by December 10.

5. **FR Doc. 2026-22936 — [Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22936/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-reforming-categorical-eligibility)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-10 | **Key deadline:** Comments due **2026-12-10** | **Tier:** **Critical**  
   **Owner:** sales — Aisha Grant  
   **Reason:** Limiting categorical SNAP eligibility to households receiving TANF “assistance” could remove eligibility based only on noncash or in-kind benefits, reducing the potential customer base.  
   **Action:** Estimate affected SNAP-volume exposure with retail partners and file comments on anticipated demand effects by December 10.

6. **FR Doc. 2026-22826 — [Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22826/pecans-grown-in-the-states-of-alabama-arkansas-arizona-california-florida-georgia-kansas-louisiana)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-09 | **Key deadline:** Comments due **2026-12-09** | **Tier:** **Critical**  
   **Owner:** sourcing — Tom Alvarez  
   **Reason:** Proposed pecan marketing-order changes to handler reporting, inter-handler transfers and assessment late fees could affect supplier administration and costs.  
   **Action:** Confirm which pecan suppliers are regulated handlers, assess contract/cost implications and coordinate any industry comments by December 9.

7. **FR Doc. 2026-22761 — [Rules of Practice and Procedure for Administrative Hearings Before the Office of Administrative Law Judges](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22761/rules-of-practice-and-procedure-for-administrative-hearings-before-the-office-of-administrative-law)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-09 | **Key deadline:** Effective **2026-12-09** | **Tier:** **Critical**  
   **Owner:** operations — Ben Kowalski  
   **Reason:** Represented parties in Department of Labor OALJ proceedings must generally use electronic filing and service, affecting any future OSHA, wage or other covered labor dispute.  
   **Action:** Have labor counsel establish eFile/eServe readiness and update litigation procedures by December 9; no plant-wide process change is otherwise needed.

8. **FR Doc. 2026-22814 — [Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of a Renewed Approval of Information Collection(s): Procedures for Transportation Workplace Drug and Alcohol Testing Programs (ICR 2105-0529)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22814/agency-information-collection-activities-requests-for-comments-clearance-of-a-renewed-approval-of)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-09 | **Key deadline:** Comments due **2027-01-08** | **Tier:** **Critical** *(deadline-driven; routine renewal)*  
   **Owner:** operations — Ben Kowalski  
   **Reason:** The renewal covers DOT Part 40 drug/alcohol-testing records and MIS/alcohol-testing forms relevant to FMCSA-regulated fleet employers.  
   **Action:** Verify the fleet’s testing records and forms remain current and submit comments by January 8 only if the renewal’s burden estimates or proposed form revisions raise issues.

9. **FR Doc. 2026-22891 — [Rules and Regulations, Series 8](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22891/rules-and-regulations-series-8)**  
   **Published:** 2026-11-10 | **Key deadline:** No new general compliance deadline; a covered NLRB petition response remains due **14 days after service** | **Tier:** **Low**  
   **Owner:** operations — Ben Kowalski  
   **Reason:** This technical correction revises and reinstates NLRB procedures at 29 CFR 102.101–102.103 but creates no new substantive plant obligation.  
   **Action:** No immediate action; have labor counsel reference the corrected provisions if an NLRB jurisdictional advisory-opinion petition arises.

items.reason: This companion order separately removes methylene chloride as a diluent in color-additive mixtures used in fruit-and-vegetable marking inks and is scheduled effective 2027-01-11.
items.action: Check produce and color-ink suppliers for the affected use and incorporate its removal into the FR Doc. 2026-22866 compliance review.

items.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
items.reason: Proposed SNAP time-limit exceptions, age coverage and geographic-waiver changes could alter customer eligibility and SNAP-supported demand.

items.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements

items.reason: Represented parties in Department of Labor OALJ proceedings must generally use electronic filing and service, affecting any future OSHA, wage or other covered labor dispute.
items.action: Have labor counsel establish eFile/eServe readiness and update litigation procedures by December 9; no plant-wide process change is otherwise needed.

items.title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of a Renewed Approval of Information Collection(s): Procedures for Transportation Workplace Drug and Alcohol Testing Programs (ICR 2105-0529)
items.reason: The routine renewal covers DOT Part 40 drug/alcohol-testing records and MIS/alcohol-testing forms relevant to FMCSA-regulated fleet employers.
items.action: Verify the fleet’s testing records and forms remain current and submit comments by January 8 only if the renewal’s burden estimates or proposed form revisions raise issues.

items.title: Rules and Regulations, Series 8
items.reason: This technical correction revises and reinstates NLRB procedures at 29 CFR 102.101–102.103 but creates no new substantive plant obligation or general compliance deadline; a covered NLRB petition response remains due 14 days after service.
items.action: No immediate action; have labor counsel reference the corrected provisions if an NLRB jurisdictional advisory-opinion petition arises.
